defects.observed: Planet labels are tiny for a 1280x720 presentation slide: the planet names ('Mercury', 'Venus', 'Earth') render at roughly 14px and the period sublabels ('4s orbit', '7s orbit', '11s orbit') at roughly 11px. They are dwarfed by the 44px title and 20px subtitle and are hard to read at presentation distance.
defects.required: Rubric item 4: text must be legible with reasonable font sizes for a presentation (body >= ~20px equivalent). Prompt requires readable labels.

defects.observed: The 'Sun' text is drawn in light/white type directly on the bright yellow-orange core of the sun gradient. In all three frames it is washed out and barely readable against the glowing fill.
defects.required: Rubric item 4: sufficient contrast, no text on top of busy graphics.

defects.observed: Static labels are parked in the gap between their own orbit ring and the next ring out, so at several timestamps the planet physically nearest a label is the wrong one. At t0 the blue Earth planet (approx 849,456) sits ~45px from the 'Venus' label (approx 826,417) while the actual Venus planet is ~55px away. At t5 the tan Venus planet (approx 683,277) sits ~57px from the 'Mercury' label while Mercury itself is ~155px away on the far side. A viewer can misattribute the name to the adjacent planet.
defects.required: Labels must clearly identify which orbit/planet they name at ALL timestamps.

defects.observed: The 'Venus' label's right edge (x approx 851) coincides with the outermost orbit ring at that height (x approx 851, y 419), so the text runs into the Earth orbit stroke rather than sitting cleanly in open space. Similarly the 'Mercury' sublabel baseline sits only ~6px above the inner orbit ring.
defects.required: Rubric items 3 and 6: no overlapping elements; labels attached cleanly to the right shapes.

defects.observed: Label placement convention is visually inconsistent in direction: Mercury's label is above its orbit, Venus's is to the right of its orbit, Earth's is below its orbit, which forces the viewer to re-derive the mapping for each ring instead of reading a uniform pattern.
defects.required: Rubric item 6: labels attached to the right shapes in an unambiguous, consistent way.

summary: The animated SVG solar system is functionally correct: sun centered, exactly three planets on three visible orbit rings, positions clearly differ across t0/t2/t5 with three distinct angular speeds (Mercury fastest, Earth slowest), all planets measured to lie on their rings, no frozen end state at t5, no console errors, and no 1280x720 overflow. Defects are in label presentation: the planet labels and period sublabels are far below presentation-legible size, the 'Sun' text has near-zero contrast on the bright solar gradient, and the static labels sit mid-gap between rings so the nearest planet to a label is the wrong one at t0 (Earth beside 'Venus') and t5 (Venus beside 'Mercury'), with the 'Venus' text also grazing the outer orbit stroke.
